subject: science
title: Day Sky, Night Sky
about: What we see in the day sky and the night sky, and how the sun and moon seem to move across it (ESS.1.1.1). NC asks children to notice the apparent movement, not explain it.
tip: Look out the same window in the morning and after dinner and talk about where the sun was each time.

cards.q: What do we see in the day sky that gives us light and heat?
What do we see in the night sky?
Can we ever see the moon in the daytime?
cards.note: Look for a pale moon on a bright day.

cards.q: When does the sun seem to come up?
When does the sun seem to go down?
In the morning the sun is low. By midday, where does the sun seem to be?
cards.note: Midday is the middle of the day. The sun seems highest then.

cards.q: Which one can hurt your eyes if you look right at it?
cards.note: Never look right at the sun.

cards.q: What kind of sky object is the sun?
cards.note: The sun is the star closest to us.

cards.q: Why do stars look so small?
cards.note: Stars are very big, but very far away.

cards.q: When can we see lots of stars?
From morning to evening, what does the sun seem to do?
cards.note: It only seems to move. We see this pattern every day.

cards.q: What shape does the sun look like in the sky?

cards.note: Day and night repeat. That is a pattern.

cards.q: The sky is dark and you see the moon. Is it day or night?
On a clear day, what color is the sky?
cards.note: Clouds are part of the day sky too.

cards.q: Watch the moon all night. What does it seem to do?
cards.note: The moon and stars seem to move too, just like the sun.
